bugs.name: Restoring Notes or Tasks revives removed relations and can create duplicate links
bugs.summary: Restoring a deleted Note or Task reactivates relations removed before deletion. If a relation was removed and re-added beforehand, Restore can revive both link rows and show duplicate activity cards.
bugs.expected: Restoring a Note or Task restores the relations present when it was deleted and leaves previously removed relations absent.
bugs.actual: A relation removed from a Note or Task and confirmed absent after reload returns after Delete and Restore, and persists after another reload. When another relation was retained, Restore brought back both the retained relation and the previously removed relation. When the same company relation is removed and re-added before deleting and restoring a Note or Task, two live links for that activity/company pair can return. The company then displays duplicate cards for the same activity and an inflated total that persists after reload.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a fresh Task. Open its full record.
Use Relations to link an existing person, then dismiss the picker to save.
Reopen Relations, uncheck that person, dismiss the picker and reload. Confirm the relation is absent.
Use the command menu to delete the Task, then choose Restore in the deleted-record banner.
Observe that the previously removed person relation returns. Reload and confirm it remains.
Repeat with a fresh Note and a company relation: link the company, unlink it, confirm its absence after reload, then delete and restore the Note.
For the duplicate-card variant, create two distinct Notes related to a fresh company. On one Note, remove its company relation and then re-add the same company.
Delete that Note, open it through the company Timeline, and choose Restore.

Return to the company Notes tab. Observe two cards for the restored Note alongside the untouched Note, producing Notes 3. Reload and confirm the duplicates persist. The same remove/re-add, delete and restore sequence also reproduces for Tasks.

bugs.name: Deleting a named related Task or Note changes its creation Timeline label to Untitled
bugs.summary: After deleting a named Task or Note created from a company, its creation entry remains in the company Timeline but identifies the activity as Untitled.
bugs.expected: After a named related Task or Note is deleted, its creation entry should either be removed from the Timeline or retain the activity’s saved name.
bugs.actual: After deletion and reload, the creation entry reads “You created a related task Untitled” or the equivalent for a Note. Opening the entry still reveals the correct deleted activity with its saved title and body. An undeleted control retains its name in the Timeline.
reproSteps: Sign in and open an existing company. From its Tasks tab, create a fresh related Task with a unique title, confirm the title with Enter, and enter body text.
Create a second named related Task in the same way and leave it undeleted as a control.
Open the first Task’s full record and use the command menu to delete it.
Return to the company, open Timeline, and reload.
Observe that the deleted Task’s creation entry remains but shows Untitled, while the undeleted Task’s entry retains its name.
Open the Untitled entry and confirm that the deleted Task still has its saved title and body.
Repeat with a fresh named related Note created from the company’s Notes tab; its creation entry also becomes Untitled after deletion and reload.

bugs.name: Refreshing newly created Notes or Tasks opens an empty title editor that can erase their saved names
bugs.summary: Reloading a newly created Note or Task can reopen its title editor with an empty draft. Committing that draft erases the saved title; the Note variant also occurs when reopening the activity from its company Timeline after the creation-page reload.
bugs.expected: Reloading or reopening a named Note or Task preserves its saved title unless the user deliberately changes it.
bugs.actual: After the creation-page reload, the title editor can appear empty although the saved name initially remains in the browser title and can be recovered by pressing Escape. Clicking outside the editor, selecting Fields, or pressing Enter can instead persist the empty title. The activity then remains unnamed after reload. The Note’s saved body survives. Controls without the creation-page reload retain their titles.
reproSteps: For the Note variant, sign in and use a mobile-width viewport. Open a company’s full record, then choose More > Notes > New note.
Enter a unique title, confirm with Enter, enter body text, and click outside the body editor to save.
Reload the Note’s creation page, then follow its company relation back to the company. Open Notes and confirm the saved title appears on its card.
Open the company Timeline and click the Note’s creation entry. Without entering a replacement title, click outside the empty Title editor. Reload and observe Untitled while the body remains.
For the Task variant, create a fresh Task, enter a unique title, confirm it with Enter, and open its full record.
Reload that Task page and observe the empty title editor. Select Fields or press Enter without entering a replacement title.
Reload or reopen the Task and confirm the previously saved title has been erased. On a fresh equivalent Task, press Escape instead to confirm the saved name is retained.

The same Note variant also reproduces when creating a standalone Note from Notes at tablet width: save its title with Enter, reload its creation page, then click outside the empty title editor or press Tab to persist the empty title. Pressing Escape instead preserves the saved name.

bugs.name: Deleting a company-related Note or Task leaves its tab total stale
bugs.summary: Deleting a Note or Task from a company’s embedded activity view removes its card but leaves the overall Notes or Tasks total unchanged until the view is reopened or refreshed.
bugs.expected: The company Notes or Tasks total should decrease when a related activity is deleted, matching the remaining cards and, for Tasks, the group count.
bugs.actual: After deleting one of two related Notes or Tasks, its card disappears but the header still shows a total of 2. Task group counts decrease correctly. Deleting the final activity can leave a total of 2 above an empty list. Reopening the tab or reloading corrects the total; the deletion itself succeeds.
reproSteps: Sign in, create a fresh company, and open its full record.
From the company Tasks tab, create two distinctly titled related Tasks.
Open one Task from the embedded view and choose Options > Delete Task.
Without refreshing or switching tabs, compare the remaining cards and group count with the overall Tasks total. One card remains and the group count decreases to 1, while the header remains Tasks 2.
Repeat from the company Notes tab with two distinctly titled related Notes. Open one and choose Options > Delete Note. One card remains, but the header still says Notes 2.
Delete the final activity to observe a stale total above an empty list. Reload or reopen the relevant tab and confirm its total corrects itself.

bugs.name: Typing in Search with a Note or Task body editor open inserts and saves the query in its body
bugs.summary: Typing into focused command-menu or navigation records Search on an open Note or Task leaves Search empty and saves the query in the activity body.
bugs.expected: Typing into focused Search filters its commands or records without changing the open activity body.
bugs.actual: With the command-menu search focused, typing a query such as Delete Note or Export Note leaves the search empty and inserts that query as activity body text. The unintended text persists after reload. Both Notes and Tasks reproduce; controls with the activity editor absent allow command search to work. Navigation records Search, including tablet/mobile bottom Search, also stays blank and inserts a saved paragraph into the mounted activity body; existing baseline content remains.
reproSteps: Sign in, create a fresh Note with a unique title and body, and open its full record with the body editor visible.
Open the record command menu, click its search input, and type a query such as Delete Note or Export Note.
Observe that the search remains empty while the typed query appears in the Note body.
Close the command menu, allow the body save to complete, then reload and confirm the unintended text remains.
Repeat with a fresh Task and its visible body editor. As a control, open the same activity’s Files tab and verify that command-menu typing stays in the search when the body editor is absent.

Additional verified variation: Use navigation records Search, including bottom Search at tablet/mobile width, with the Note or Task Home body editor mounted. Create a fresh Note with a saved baseline body and open its full record Home tab. At tablet/mobile width, click bottom navigation Search and focus Type anything. Type a distinctive query. Observe the empty Search input and unchanged initial results. Close Search, wait for autosave and reload. Confirm the query was added to the Note body while its baseline remains. Repeat on a second fresh Note and a fresh Task. Control: use navigation Search from the Notes list, a Company record, or the activity Timeline without its editor mounted; the query stays in Search.

bugs.name: Opening a related record’s Tasks tab hides the open Task’s saved assignee
bugs.summary: Viewing a related Person’s or Company’s Tasks tab makes an already saved assignee disappear from the open Task, falsely displaying it as unassigned until reload.
bugs.expected: Opening a related record’s Tasks tab preserves the open Task’s displayed saved assignee.
bugs.actual: A Task initially displays its saved assignee. After opening a related Person’s Tasks tab in a side panel, the main Task’s Assignee field becomes an empty placeholder. The assignment remains saved, changing Status during the blank display does not clear it, and reloading restores the assignee. The same display failure was reproduced through a related Company’s Tasks tab.
reproSteps: Sign in, create a fresh Task, and open its full record.
Assign an existing workspace member and reload to confirm the assignee remains saved and visible.
Relate an existing Person to the Task and reload. Confirm the assignee is still displayed.
Click the related Person to open their side panel, then select its Tasks tab.
Observe that the original Task’s Assignee field now displays an empty placeholder even though no assignment edit was made.
Reload the Task and confirm the original assignee returns. Opening the Person’s Home or Timeline instead of Tasks preserves the displayed assignee.

bugs.name: Previous Calendar event navigation skips tied-position records or stays on the same event
bugs.summary: The Previous Calendar event action can skip adjacent records or remain on the current event when multiple events share the same sort position, while Next traverses them correctly.
bugs.expected: Previous opens the immediately preceding Calendar event in the current view’s ordering, including when records share the same sort position.
bugs.actual: In a three-event view ordered A, B, C with tied positions, Next visits A, B, C correctly, but Previous from C opens A and skips B. Previous from the first tied event can remain on that event instead of navigating correctly. Seeded later events also jump back to Team Standup rather than the adjacent event. Controls with distinct positions navigate correctly.
reproSteps: Sign in and open Calendar events through the command menu. Use the default ordering, in which seeded events share the same position value.
Open a later event such as Strategic Planning Workshop or Training Session, then choose Navigate to previous Calendar event.
Observe that navigation jumps back to Team Standup instead of the immediately preceding record in the view.
Use Next to verify that adjacent events can be reached in the forward direction, then compare Previous from a later event.

For a focused control, use a view containing three events with tied positions. Confirm Next traverses A, B, C, then choose Previous from C and observe it skip B. Distinct-position events navigate correctly.

bugs.name: Unlinking a company from a Task or Note is described as deleting the activity in Timeline
bugs.summary: Removing a Task’s or Note’s company relation creates a company Timeline entry saying the activity was deleted even though it remains live.
bugs.expected: The company Timeline should describe removal of the relation rather than deletion of the still-existing Task or Note.
bugs.actual: After the company is unchecked in a Task’s Relations picker, the company Timeline says “You deleted a related task.” The Task remains available, its Relations field is empty, and clicking the Timeline entry opens the live Task. Unlinking a Note produces the corresponding “deleted a related note” wording. The incorrect wording persists after navigation.
reproSteps: Sign in, create a fresh company, and create a named Task related to it.
Open the Task’s full record and edit Relations. Uncheck the company and dismiss the picker to save; do not use Delete Task.
Return to the company and open Timeline. Observe the entry saying You deleted a related task.
Click the Timeline entry and confirm the Task still exists and opens normally, with the company relation removed.
Repeat with a named Note and remove only its company relation. Observe the equivalent deletion wording in the company Timeline.

bugs.name: Deleting activity attachments hides saved relations and can create duplicate links
bugs.summary: Deleting an attachment hides a Note’s or Task’s existing relation chips. The relation picker then incorrectly shows those links as unselected; reselecting one on a Note can create a second persisted link to the same record.
bugs.expected: Deleting an attachment preserves the activity’s existing relation display and picker selections. Selecting an already related record should not create a duplicate link.
bugs.actual: After an attachment is deleted, previously visible Note or Task relations disappear even though the links remain saved; reloading restores them. Before reloading, the picker shows an existing relation as unchecked. Selecting that company again on a Note creates another live link, and two relation chips for the same company remain after reload. Controls without attachment deletion preserve the correct selection and a single link.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a fresh Note. Use the normal Relations picker to link an existing company and confirm that its chip is visible.
Upload a small disposable file through the Note’s Files tab, then delete that attachment.
Return to the Note body and Relations display without refreshing. Observe that the saved company chip is missing.
Open the Relations picker. Observe that the company already linked to the Note appears unchecked.
Select that company again and dismiss the picker to save.
Reload the Note and observe two chips for the same company; the duplicate link also remains visible in a separately reloaded view.

As a control, repeat attachment deletion on a fresh related Note but reload before reselecting any relation. The original single link returns. Task relation chips also disappear after attachment deletion, but the persisted duplicate-link consequence was verified on Notes.

bugs.name: Company and Person Tasks tabs show raw status codes and null as group headings
bugs.summary: Related Task lists group records under internal status values instead of the readable labels used by the same Tasks’ status fields and pickers.
bugs.expected: Task group headings use the readable status labels shown in the status field and picker, including No Status for an unset status.
bugs.actual: Company and Person Tasks views display headings such as TODO, IN_PROGRESS, DONE and literal null. The same Tasks’ fields and pickers display To do, In progress, Done and No Status. Changing status moves the Task into the corresponding raw-value group; editing and completing Tasks still works.
reproSteps: Sign in, create a fresh company, and open its Tasks tab.
Create a related Task with a unique title and observe its group heading, such as TODO.
Open the Task and use its Status picker to select In progress. Return to the company Tasks tab and observe IN_PROGRESS as the group heading.
Clear the Task status using No Status, then return to the company Tasks view and observe a group headed null.
Compare the raw headings with the readable labels in the same Task’s Status field and picker. The same mismatch also reproduces in a related Person’s Tasks tab.

bugs.name: Metadata-only calendar sharing exposes meeting links and locations
bugs.summary: Calendar events shared as Metadata expose meeting URLs and locations to another workspace member even though the settings promise to share only date and participants.
bugs.expected: A viewer whose calendar access is Metadata sees only the event date and participants; meeting links and locations remain restricted.
bugs.actual: For a Metadata-only viewer, the company Calendar tab shows a locked Not shared event row that does not open. Opening the event’s full record URL nevertheless reveals its meeting link and location while the description remains restricted. The exposed fields remain visible after reload. The calendar owner can view the complete event as expected.
reproSteps: Use a calendar owner’s account with calendar sharing set to Metadata. Choose an event with a nonempty meeting link and location, open its full record, and copy the record URL.
In a separate browser session, sign in as another workspace member who does not own that calendar and has only Metadata visibility for the event.
Open the related company’s Calendar tab. Confirm the event appears as a locked Not shared row and does not open when clicked.
Navigate to the copied full record URL and inspect the meeting link and location. Observe that they are readable although the event description remains restricted.
Reload and confirm those details remain readable. Compare with the owner account, which correctly sees the complete event.

bugs.name: A stale Note or Task main editor overwrites completed Body-field saves
bugs.summary: Saving the Body field through its popup updates the stored body and field preview, but leaves the main Note or Task editor showing the old content. Editing that stale document then overwrites the completed popup save.
bugs.expected: After a Body-field edit is saved, the main editor reflects the saved content so subsequent edits preserve that change.
bugs.actual: The Body preview and a separately opened record show the new saved text, while the already-open main editor still shows the original body. Typing in that stale editor saves the old body plus the new typing, replacing the completed popup change. Reload confirms the newer popup text is lost. Both Notes and Tasks reproduce; popup-only and main-only save controls retain their changes.
reproSteps: Sign in, create a fresh Note with an initial body such as Original body, and allow that body to save.
Keep its main body editor open. Open the Body field’s edit popup, replace the body with Updated body, dismiss the popup, and allow the save to complete.
Observe the Body field preview showing Updated body while the main editor still shows Original body. Open the same record in a separate tab to confirm Updated body has already been saved.
Return to the original tab and type additional text in the stale main editor without refreshing or switching record tabs.
Allow that edit to save, then reload. Observe Original body plus the added text, with the completed Updated body change overwritten.
Repeat with a fresh Task. As a control, save a popup edit and reload without editing the stale main editor; the popup’s new body persists.

bugs.name: Opening a new note immediately after typing permanently loses its body
bugs.summary: The note side panel does not flush pending body edits when Open navigates to the full record. Reproduced twice; waiting before Open preserves the content.
bugs.expected: Open should preserve the body currently entered in the note side panel.
bugs.actual: The entered text is visible before Open, but the full note opens with an empty body. It remains empty after waiting and reloading.
reproSteps: Sign in and open Notes from the workspace navigation.
Click New Note.
Enter a unique note title such as QA Notes Quick Open Race and press Enter.
Type Expected body persists into the note body editor.
Immediately click Open at the side-panel footer.
Wait for the full note page to load, then reload it.
Observe the note body is empty and the entered content has been lost.

bugs.name: Slash-command selection leaves a literal slash in note content
bugs.summary: Selecting a block type from the rich-text slash menu retains the command-trigger slash and places the cursor before it. Reported variant (mo-30m-twenty-4): Selecting Heading 1 in a new dashboard’s Rich Text widget formats the text but leaves the slash command trigger visible at the end of the heading, including after saving and leaving edit mode. Count this as the same reference rather than a separate bug.
bugs.expected: Selecting Heading 1, Bullet List, or Check List should consume the slash trigger and allow typing clean block content.
bugs.actual: Selecting Heading 1 then typing 'QA heading text' produces 'QA heading text/' in the heading. Bullet List produces 'QA bullet/', which remains after reloading.
reproSteps: Sign in and open a note's full detail page.
Clear the body editor.
Type '/' to open the slash-command menu.
Click Heading 1.
Type 'QA heading text'.
Observe that the heading contains 'QA heading text/' with an unwanted trailing slash.
Repeat with Bullet List, type 'QA bullet', allow autosave, and reload; the list item still contains 'QA bullet/'.
Reported variant (mo-30m-twenty-4): Start signed in as the authorized Tim Apple user using the supplied saved authentication state.
Reported variant (mo-30m-twenty-4): Open Dashboards from the workspace navigation at the app.
Reported variant (mo-30m-twenty-4): Create a new dashboard titled MOEXP_RichTextSlash_7f3a and save it.
Reported variant (mo-30m-twenty-4): Choose Add widget, then Rich Text, and click its content area.
Reported variant (mo-30m-twenty-4): Type `/` to open the visible command menu, select Heading 1, and type `MOEXP heading`.
Reported variant (mo-30m-twenty-4): Observe the rendered heading as `MOEXP heading/`, then save the dashboard and verify the slash remains visible in the saved dashboard view.

bugs.name: New mailing lists cannot be named through the creation or record UI
bugs.summary: New List creates an Untitled record, but its table cell, side panel and full record provide no name editor. Lists created from campaign recipient selection are likewise left named Untitled list.
bugs.expected: Creating a mailing list should allow entering a name so multiple lists can be distinguished when choosing campaign recipients.
bugs.actual: New List immediately creates Untitled. Its side-panel title is a navigation link, the full record contains only system fields and Members, and double-clicking the table Name cell opens the same panel. Multiple created lists remain indistinguishable Untitled entries.
reproSteps: Sign in, open Command Menu, and choose Go to Lists.
Click New List.
Observe an Untitled list is created and its side-panel heading is a navigation link with no name editor.
Click Open at the panel footer; observe the full list has only creation/update system fields and Members, with no Name input.
Return to Lists and double-click the Name cell; observe the same panel opens rather than a name editor.
Create another list and observe both appear as Untitled.
Alternate path: Compose Campaign > To > Add New creates Untitled list without a naming input.

bugs.name: Opportunity Timeline activity descriptions are clipped without a reveal option at mobile width
bugs.summary: At 390×844, the new opportunity’s Timeline update and creation descriptions are visibly cut off at the right edge, and scrolling or tapping does not reveal their remaining text.
bugs.expected: The Timeline activity descriptions should remain readable in full at 390×844, or provide a visible way to reveal the clipped text.
bugs.actual: The update description ends visibly mid-text at “Mobile Timeline Readabili…” and the creation description ends at “Q7x,” omitting “Kestrel Opportunity.” Horizontal scrolling did not move the Timeline or page; tapping the entries did not expand them. A horizontal drag only selected the visible text.
reproSteps: Set the browser viewport to 390×844 and load the authorized saved session for Tim Apple in the Apple workspace; do not change authentication details.
Navigate to /objects/opportunities?viewId=509937ae-e50c-4c10-89ec-e0ae0f1c1a2a.
Open the top-right Command Menu and choose “Create new Opportunity” to create a fresh record; do not use a seeded or another user's opportunity.
Set its name to “Mobile Timeline Readability Check 2026-02-17 Q7x Kestrel Opportunity” and press Enter to save the name.
Open the record’s Timeline tab and wait for its name-update and creation activity entries to appear.

Observe at 390×844: the update narrative is cut off after “Mobile Timeline Readabili…” and the creation narrative after “Q7x.” Scroll horizontally over the Timeline and the page, tap each entry, and drag horizontally over the creation text. No action reveals the remaining text; the drag only selects the visible portion.

bugs.name: Browser Back clears company Timeline fragment without switching back to Home
bugs.summary: Browser Back removes the new company’s Timeline fragment but leaves the Timeline view selected; refreshing the restored hashless URL then displays Home.
bugs.expected: After browser Back restores the company’s pre-Timeline, hashless record URL, the visible tab and content should also return to Home.
bugs.actual: At 390×844, selecting Timeline added a fragment to the company URL. Browser Back removed it, but Timeline remained selected and its activity feed remained visible for at least five seconds. Refreshing at that same hashless URL displayed Home.
reproSteps: At a 390×844 viewport, use the supplied saved authentication session for Tim Apple in the Apple workspace; do not include or expose the saved-state path. Open /objects/companies?viewId=76ab92b8-5254-4f7c-9ed1-35a713200052.

Open the top-right Command Menu, select Create new Company, and give the fresh record the unique name MoTimelineBackSync-Repro-20260630-6381. Confirm the new record opens with Home selected at /object/company/f6f7f484-6555-473f-971b-8aca6c742091.
Select the company’s Timeline tab. Confirm the URL becomes /object/company/f6f7f484-6555-473f-971b-8aca6c742091#9a5c41a2-fd97-44e2-9091-c5857e07165b and the Timeline feed is visible.
Press the browser Back button once. The URL returns to /object/company/f6f7f484-6555-473f-971b-8aca6c742091, but Timeline remains selected and its feed stays visible after waiting five seconds.

bugs.name: Restricted calendar event titles are revealed in side panels and relation lists
bugs.summary: Calendar event titles hidden by permissions in the main event table/full page are revealed in side-panel headings and Event ID relation chips in participants and channel-association lists.
bugs.expected: Every UI representation of an event should honor its title restriction.
bugs.actual: The event table/full page shows FIELD_RESTRICTED_ADDITIONAL_PERMISSIONS_REQUIRED, but the side panel reveals Project Planning Session and Code Review Session. Calendar event participants and Calendar Channel Event Associations also display these restricted titles in Event ID cells.
reproSteps: Sign in with tim@apple.dev and open Command Menu > Go to Calendar events.
Find the restricted event starting Nov 11, 2026 8:00 AM; its Title is FIELD_RESTRICTED_ADDITIONAL_PERMISSIONS_REQUIRED.
Click that title and observe Project Planning Session in the side-panel heading.
Click Open and observe the full page title is restricted again.
Return and open the restricted Oct 16, 2026 10:00 AM row; its side panel reveals Code Review Session.
Open Command Menu > Go to Calendar event participants and observe these titles in Event ID cells.
Open Command Menu > Go to Calendar Channel Event Associations and observe external_event_3@calendar.com and external_event_5@calendar.com expose the same event titles.

bugs.name: Annual Revenue drops the decimal separator and saves a hundredfold amount
bugs.summary: Typing a decimal currency amount in company Annual Revenue or Opportunity Amount drops the decimal separator and saves a larger amount.
bugs.expected: The saved revenue should preserve the entered amount 1234.56, or reject unsupported decimals clearly rather than changing its magnitude.
bugs.actual: Character-by-character input of 1234.56 saves 123,456 and displays about $123.5k. Reload preserves the inflated amount; integer input 1234 round-trips correctly.
reproSteps: Open Companies and create a fresh company. Open its full record.
Double-click its initially empty Annual Revenue field.
Type 1234.56 character by character and press Enter.
Observe that the field and Timeline display about $123.5k. Reload and reopen the editor; the saved value is 123,456.
On a fresh company, type the integer 1234 and verify it remains 1234 after reload.

bugs.name: Tablet record opening leaves expanded workspace navigation covering the loaded note
bugs.summary: Expanded desktop workspace navigation carries into tablet layout and covers a Note or Task opened from a related activity card.
bugs.expected: Opening the note card shows its note content/details.
bugs.actual: After resizing from desktop to 768px with navigation expanded, opening a related activity closes the company panel but leaves workspace navigation covering the loaded record. One navigation toggle reveals the correctly saved content. Native mobile with navigation closed works.
reproSteps: At desktop width, keep workspace navigation expanded and create a fresh company-related Note with a title and body.
Open the Note full page, follow its company relation, and open Notes in the company side panel.
Resize to 768×1024 CSS pixels while leaving navigation expanded.
Click the Note card. Observe that the company panel closes and workspace navigation covers the loaded Note.
Toggle Main navigation once; the Note and its saved content become visible. Compare opening the card with navigation already collapsed.

bugs.name: Mobile Note/Task Body popup clips editable text and its expand control beyond the viewport
bugs.summary: The rich text popup opened from a note or task Body field is wider than a mobile screen, clipping the editor and putting its expand button outside the usable viewport.
bugs.expected: At390 CSS pixels wide, the Body popup and controls should fit the screen or provide usable scrolling to reach them.
bugs.actual: At 390px width, the Body popup is 480px wide and extends beyond the visible right edge. Editable text is clipped and the expand control is offscreen. The full Note or Task editor remains usable and stored text is intact; universal click or keyboard failure is not claimed.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Note with a long line of body text and wait for saving to finish.
Set the viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels and close the navigation drawer.
On the Home tab, click the Body value under Fields to open the popup.
Observe the clipped editable text and offscreen expand control; sideways scrolling does not make the whole popup fit.
Compare at desktop width and repeat on a fresh Task.

bugs.name: Notes and Tasks containing record mentions cannot export to PDF
bugs.summary: PDF export fails for Notes and Tasks whose bodies contain a supported record mention, while plain-text bodies export successfully.
bugs.expected: Export to PDF produces a PDF for supported Note and Task body content, including record mentions.
bugs.actual: Export to PDF repeatedly shows An error occurred and produces no download for bodies containing a company or person mention. Plain-text bodies export successfully, and removing the mention restores PDF export. CSV export succeeds for the same mention content.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Note and enter plain body text. Wait for saving to finish.
Use its command menu to Export to PDF and confirm a download succeeds.
Edit the body to add a supported @mention of an existing company or person. Wait for saving to finish.
Export to PDF again. Observe An error occurred and no PDF download.
Remove the mention, save, and repeat the export; the PDF download succeeds. Repeat the mention variant on a fresh Task.

bugs.name: Mobile record Tasks rows leave only a few task-title characters visible
bugs.summary: Narrow company and person Tasks rows squeeze task titles to only a few visible characters, especially when a due date and body preview are present.
bugs.expected: Task rows allocate enough readable title text to identify the task without opening each row.
bugs.actual: At 390px, fresh dated tasks with body previews can show only one or a few title characters before an ellipsis. The exact visible count varies. Wider full-page views expose more of the same saved title, and opening the Task reveals the full name.
reproSteps: Open a company full page at 390×844 CSS pixels.
Create two related Tasks with distinct descriptive titles, due dates, and body text. Save and return to the company Tasks tab.
Observe how little title text remains visible beside the date and body preview; do not require every row to show exactly one character.
Open each Task to confirm its full saved title is intact.
Compare the Tasks tab at desktop width and repeat with a Person record.

bugs.name: Restricted calendar Description displays raw FIELD_RESTRICTED_ADDITIONAL_PERMISSIONS_REQUIRED code
bugs.summary: A teammate opening a restricted calendar event sees an internal permission error constant in its Description field.
bugs.expected: A restricted Description should show a readable permission message or an appropriate empty state.
bugs.actual: As Jony Ive, the seeded One-on-One Meeting General tab displayed FIELD_RESTRICTED_ADDITIONAL_PERMISSIONS_REQUIRED in Description.
reproSteps: Sign in as the configured teammate Jony Ive.
Open the seeded One-on-One Meeting calendar event as a full record.
Inspect General → Description and observe the raw FIELD_RESTRICTED_ADDITIONAL_PERMISSIONS_REQUIRED code.

bugs.name: Linkedin URL entered with Enter disappears after refresh
bugs.summary: A company Linkedin URL shows a preview after Enter but is empty after refreshing the record.
bugs.expected: Committing the Linkedin edit with Enter should persist the displayed URL or visibly explain why it was not saved.
bugs.actual: After entering https://www.linkedin.com/company/qa-fields/?test=1 and pressing Enter, the qa-fields preview appeared. Refreshing left Linkedin empty, with no corresponding Timeline update or visible validation warning.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Company and open its record.
Edit Linkedin, enter https://www.linkedin.com/company/qa-fields/?test=1, and press Enter.
Observe the qa-fields preview, then refresh the record.
Observe that Linkedin is empty and no matching Timeline update or validation warning explains the loss.

bugs.name: Escape commits Annual Revenue edit instead of cancelling it
bugs.summary: Pressing Escape in an Annual Revenue editor commits the pending amount instead of preserving the previously saved value.
bugs.expected: Escape should cancel the pending Annual Revenue edit and retain its previously saved value.
bugs.actual: A saved EUR -250 amount became EUR 16 in both the field and Timeline after typing 1e6, which the input filtered to 16, and pressing Escape.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Company and save Annual Revenue as EUR -250.
Reopen Annual Revenue and replace the amount by typing 1e6; observe that the input contains 16.
Press Escape to close the editor.
Observe EUR 16 in the field and its Timeline update instead of the previous EUR -250.

bugs.name: Escape saves edited company Address instead of cancelling
bugs.summary: Pressing Escape in a company Address editor saves a pending Address 1 change and creates a Timeline update.
bugs.expected: Escape should cancel the pending Address edit and preserve the previously saved address.
bugs.actual: After changing Address 1 from 17 QA Avenue to CANCELLED STREET and pressing Escape, the editor closed and CANCELLED STREET appeared in both the Address field and Timeline.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Company and save Address as 17 QA Avenue, Montréal, Québec, H2Y 1C6, Canada.
Reopen Address and replace Address 1 with CANCELLED STREET.
Press Escape to close the editor.
Observe that the changed street was saved in the Address field and activity Timeline.

bugs.name: Record CSV exports contain only Id when list-column state is uninitialized
bugs.summary: A record CSV export routed through the index exporter produces only Id when that object’s list-column state has not initialized. Direct loading, refreshing, or opening a related Calendar event before visiting its list can reach this state.
bugs.expected: Record CSV export should include the applicable configured columns without requiring the user to visit the object list first.
bugs.actual: Two fresh notes per judge exported only Id and the record UUID after refresh or direct loading, despite saved titles and bodies remaining visible. The same notes exported populated fields from the list or before refresh. Company and Task record-page exports also produced Id-only files. Follow-up Calendar event reproductions exported only Id after opening through a Company Calendar tab before visiting the Calendar events list. Visiting that list made the same record export include 11 columns; reloading reproduced Id-only output.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a fresh Note with a unique title and body.
Allow the content to save, open the Note record page, and reload it. Confirm the title and body remain visible.
Open the record’s command menu and choose Export Note. Inspect the downloaded CSV and observe only the Id header and record UUID, with no Title or Body columns.
As a control, export the same Note from the Notes list with the record selected; observe populated Title and Body columns.
Alternatively, open the Note from the list and export before refreshing; observe populated fields. Reload the same record page and repeat the failing export.
Repeat with a second saved Note. Equivalent directly loaded Company and Task record pages demonstrate the shared export path.

For the Calendar variant, open a Company, choose Calendar and open an event before visiting the Calendar events list. Export from its record menu and observe Id-only output. Visit the Calendar events list and repeat the same export to observe populated configured columns.

bugs.name: Company side-panel activity context redirects main-page Note and Task creation
bugs.summary: Opening another company’s Notes or Tasks in the side panel overwrites the main company’s activity header and makes its New action create records linked only to the side-panel company.
bugs.expected: The main company’s activity header and New action remain scoped to that company while another company is open in the side panel.
bugs.actual: Company B’s side-panel Notes or Tasks overwrite Company A’s main activity header state. New on A’s main header creates a Note or Task linked only to B, persisting after reload. Equal counts can conceal the targeting failure.
reproSteps: Create uniquely named Companies A and B with distinguishable activity counts.
Open A on its full record page and select Notes.
Open B in the side panel and select Notes.
Click New in A’s main Notes header, save a uniquely named note, reload and inspect its company relation: it links only to B.
Repeat with Tasks on both records; New from A’s main Tasks header also targets B.
Control: creating from A without a side panel, or with B’s side panel on Home, targets A correctly.

bugs.name: Editing a stale Body-field popover overwrites the main note's recently saved paragraph
bugs.summary: An already-open Body-field popover retains an old document and overwrites completed main-editor saves when edited.
bugs.expected: An untouched Body popover should reflect completed main-editor saves before a subsequent edit, preserving already-saved content.
bugs.actual: The main editor saves new text successfully, but an already-open Body popover remains stale. Editing that popover saves its older document and removes the main-editor additions; reload confirms persisted loss.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Note with an initial body and let it save.
Open its Body-field popover and keep it mounted.
Add distinctive text through the main body editor and wait for saving to finish. Confirm the new body through a separate tab or account.
Edit the still-open stale Body popover and allow its save to complete.
Reload the record and confirm the previously saved main-editor additions are gone.
Repeat with a Task. Control: open the popover only after the main-editor save; subsequent editing preserves both changes.

bugs.name: Resizing an open TXT or PDF attachment preview across the mobile breakpoint blanks its content
bugs.summary: Crossing the 768px layout breakpoint blanks an already-rendered TXT or PDF attachment preview until it is closed and reopened.
bugs.expected: An open attachment preview should retain its rendered content when the viewport crosses the mobile breakpoint.
bugs.actual: TXT or PDF content disappears after crossing the breakpoint while filename, Download and Close remain available. Returning to the original width does not restore it; closing and reopening does. Downloads retain the original bytes.
reproSteps: Attach a genuine TXT or PDF file to a fresh Note or Company and open its preview. Wait until content renders.
Resize the viewport across the 768px mobile breakpoint.
Observe that attachment content becomes blank while the dialog controls remain. Resize back and observe that content does not recover.
Close and reopen the preview to recover its rendered content.
Controls: resize within the same layout or freshly open the preview at either width; verify its content renders. Download and compare the file to confirm it remains intact.

bugs.name: Ctrl+K in selected Note or Task text opens both link editing and the global command menu
bugs.summary: The advertised rich-text link shortcut also triggers the global command menu, overlapping editing controls or closing an existing Task side panel.
bugs.expected: Ctrl+K with editor text selected should open link editing without also opening the global command menu or closing the active record panel.
bugs.actual: Desktop Ctrl+K opens Edit URL and the command panel together; at tablet width formatting controls overlap the fullscreen command menu. An already-open Task side panel can close. No saved-body loss was established.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Note or Task with saved body text and select a word in its editor.
Press Ctrl+K, the advertised link shortcut.
At desktop width observe link editing and the global command panel together. At tablet width observe editor formatting controls overlapping the global menu.
Repeat in an already-open Task side panel and observe that the global toggle can close that panel.
Controls: use Ctrl+B to format without opening the menu, or click the desktop link-toolbar button to open link editing alone. Ctrl+K outside the editor opens the ordinary global menu.

bugs.name: Renaming a favorited record leaves its sidebar label and tooltip stale across reloads
bugs.summary: A completed record rename does not refresh the favorite’s cached sidebar label or tooltip, including after ordinary reload.
bugs.expected: A favorite should display the current saved record name after renaming and reload, while continuing to navigate to that record.
bugs.actual: Record header, breadcrumb and index display the saved new name, but the expanded sidebar favorite and collapsed tooltip retain the old name across reloads. Clicking the favorite still opens the correct record.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Task with a distinctive title and add it to Favorites.
Rename the Task and wait for saving to complete. Confirm its header, breadcrumb and index show the new title.
Compare the favorite’s expanded sidebar label and collapsed-sidebar tooltip; both still show the old title.
Reload and observe the stale favorite name persists while the record title remains correctly saved.
Controls: favorite a record only after renaming to get the correct label; remove and re-add the affected favorite or clear the disposable browser metadata cache and reload to recover.

bugs.name: A narrow Company Timeline hides the related Task or Note identity beside a long timestamp
bugs.summary: Long timestamps in narrow Company side-panel Timeline rows can collapse the related Task or Note name to zero width and clip its activity type.
bugs.expected: A saved related-activity event should retain a readable Task or Note identity in the supported Company side-panel layout.
bugs.actual: The creation event can show only “You created a related…” while the Task or Note name has zero rendered width. Shorter timestamps or wider/full-page layouts reveal the title. The saved activity and title remain intact.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Company and a distinctly named related Task or Note.
Open the Company Timeline in a narrow side panel and inspect the related-activity creation event.
When the timestamp is long, such as less than a minute ago, observe the related title collapse and activity description clip.
Compare the same event in a wider panel or full Company page to confirm the title is saved and readable there.
Control: compare a short now timestamp, which leaves more space for the related title.

bugs.name: Invalid saved Domain edits stay open without any validation explanation
bugs.summary: Explicitly saving an invalid edit to a saved Company Domain is refused without a validation explanation, toast or inline message.
bugs.expected: When Enter or the checkmark refuses an invalid Domain edit, the editor should explain the validation problem. A particular red-outline styling is not required.
bugs.actual: Replacing a saved valid URL with invalid text and pressing Enter/checkmark leaves the editor open with no explanation, toast or red outline. Correcting to a valid URL saves and closes it. Escape or reload preserves the previous saved URL.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Company and save a valid Domain URL.
Edit that saved value to invalid text and press Enter or the checkmark.
Observe that the editor stays open without an explanatory inline message or toast.
Correct to a valid URL and confirm the editor saves and closes. Alternatively use Escape/reload to recover the previous saved URL.

bugs.name: Calendar all-day summary disagrees with event-detail timestamps
bugs.summary: A calendar event marked all-day displays All day in its record Calendar summary but specific daytime start/end times in its details.
bugs.expected: The Calendar summary and event details should consistently communicate whether the event is all-day or scheduled for specific times.
bugs.actual: An existing seeded workshop is labeled All day in Calendar while its details show specific daytime Start Date and End Date values. Independent reviews reproduce the inconsistency on equivalent untouched seeded workshops and fresh contradictory setup records. Valid midnight-aligned all-day and timed controls are consistent.
reproSteps: Open a Company with an existing seeded all-day workshop whose stored start or end timestamp is not aligned to its all-day boundaries.
Open the Company Calendar tab and observe the event summary labeled All day.
Open that same event and compare its displayed Start Date and End Date with the summary.
Compare a valid midnight-aligned all-day event and a normal timed event; both show consistent schedules.

bugs.name: Note and Task PDF exports corrupt Japanese text while preserving saved source content
bugs.summary: PDF export renders saved Japanese characters as missing or corrupted glyphs.
bugs.expected: Exported PDFs should preserve readable Japanese text from the saved Note or Task body.
bugs.actual: A saved and reloaded body containing café 日本語 😀 exports with correct accented Latin and emoji but missing, overlapping or garbage Japanese glyphs. Independent rendering of downloaded PDF bytes confirms generation damage. Saved source text remains correct.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Note containing café 日本語 😀 and save it. Reload to verify the source body.
Export the Note to PDF and inspect the downloaded PDF in a working renderer. Compare the Japanese glyphs with the saved body.
Repeat with a second fresh Note and a Task. Compare accented Latin, emoji, Greek and Cyrillic controls.

bugs.name: Deleting an imported Calendar event without a channel association silently leaves the event unchanged
bugs.summary: The Calendar Delete command closes without deleting a visible imported event or displaying feedback.
bugs.expected: Deleting a supported imported Calendar event should remove it or explain why deletion is unavailable.
bugs.actual: Delete Calendar event closes the command panel, but imported events without calendar-channel associations remain after reload. No deletion mutation is sent. Notes controls delete normally; associating the event with a calendar channel makes the UI deletion succeed.
reproSteps: Import a fresh Calendar event through the CSV importer without assigning a calendar-channel association.
Open the imported event’s record page and choose Delete Calendar event.
Reload and confirm the record remains without a deletion error or explanation.
Repeat with a second imported event. Compare deleting a Note and an event associated with a calendar channel.

bugs.name: Rejected Email edits provide no explanatory validation feedback
bugs.summary: Explicitly saving an invalid Email leaves the editor open without explaining why the edit was rejected.
bugs.expected: An invalid Email edit rejected after Enter or the save checkmark should display an explanatory validation message.
bugs.actual: After editing a saved valid email to not-an-email and pressing Enter or the checkmark, the editor remains open without a message or toast. The previously saved valid email remains intact; valid corrections save normally.
reproSteps: Create a Person with a valid saved email and reopen its Email editor.
Replace the email with not-an-email and press Enter or the save checkmark.
Observe that the editor remains open without an explanatory validation message.
Correct it to another valid email and verify that saving closes the editor and persists after reload.

bugs.name: Restoring a Person or Company leaves saved Notes hidden behind an empty state
bugs.summary: After deleting and restoring a Person or Company with saved Notes, the Notes panel can show Notes 1 and No notes until refetched.
bugs.expected: Restoring a record should display its saved associated Notes consistently with the panel count.
bugs.actual: The deleted banner disappears, but the saved note card remains hidden behind No notes while Notes 1 remains. Switching tabs or reloading restores the card; no saved data loss was observed.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Person with a titled Note containing saved body text. Close the editor and reload to confirm the note card appears.
With Notes open, delete the Person through its command menu, then click Restore in the deleted-record banner.
Observe Notes 1 alongside the No notes empty state, with the saved card absent.
Switch to Tasks and back to Notes, or reload, and verify the saved card returns. Repeat on a second fresh Person; Companies can also reproduce.

bugs.name: Note Body preview drops later inline text fragments within one paragraph
bugs.summary: The Note Body field and list preview hide later text runs in the same paragraph even though the saved body is complete.
bugs.expected: Formatting a word or inserting a workflow variable within a single paragraph should not remove the remaining inline text from its Body preview.
bugs.actual: A paragraph such as Alpha plain, bold BoldMiddle, and omega tail previews only Alpha plain in Fields Body and the list Body cell. The Note editor and saved content retain the full paragraph. Single-run plain text previews correctly.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Note with one paragraph containing plain text, a bold middle word, and a plain-text suffix. Save and reload.
Compare its Note editor with Fields > Body and the table Body cell. Observe that only the first inline text fragment appears in the previews.
Compare a fresh Note with the same content as one plain-text run; its preview includes the complete line.
A workflow Create Record or Create or Update Record Body containing a variable and adjacent literal text also creates multiple inline fragments and reproduces the same preview omission.

bugs.name: Open Opportunity Calendar keeps its old empty results after linking a company with meetings
bugs.summary: Linking an Opportunity to a company with meetings while its Calendar tab is open leaves Calendar showing no events until the tab is remounted or the page reloaded.
bugs.expected: An Opportunity Calendar should show the meeting history of its currently linked company after the relation edit is saved.
bugs.actual: An unlinked Opportunity initially shows Calendar 0 and No Events. Setting Company to a company with known meetings saves correctly, but Calendar remains empty. Reopening Calendar or reloading displays those meetings while retaining the same saved company. Linking the company before first opening Calendar works.
reproSteps: Use a company with known Calendar meetings and create a fresh Opportunity without a Company or Point of Contact.
Open its Calendar tab and confirm the empty state.
While keeping Calendar open, set Company to the company with meetings and wait for the relation save to finish.
Observe Calendar still showing no events despite the saved company.
Switch away and back to Calendar, or reload. Observe the previously missing company meetings.
Control: link that company on a fresh Opportunity before first opening Calendar; the meetings appear immediately.

bugs.name: Cleared Company Domain and Linkedin values render blank instead of Empty in Timeline
bugs.summary: Clearing a Company Domain Name or Linkedin saves correctly, but its Timeline row shows only the field label and arrow instead of identifying the new value as Empty.
bugs.expected: A cleared field should be labeled Empty in Timeline, consistently with cleared Address/text controls and the maintainer’s explicit empty-value display behavior.
bugs.actual: After saving and clearing a domain, reload leaves the record field correctly empty while expanded Timeline says Domain Name followed by an arrow and no value. Company Linkedin also reproduces. A cleared Address in the same update card correctly displays Empty.
reproSteps: Create a disposable Company and save a valid Domain Name.
Clear the domain through its normal editor, commit, and reload.
Open Timeline and expand the update. Observe Domain Name followed by an arrow with no value or Empty label.
Control: save or replace a nonempty domain and verify Timeline displays it. Clear Address and compare its explicit Empty label.
Repeat on another fresh Company. A separate user clearing an already-saved domain produces the same blank value in a separate activity row, distinguishing the defect from update-card grouping.

bugs.name: Permanent Person or Company destruction leaves a stale deleted record page with Restore controls
bugs.summary: Destroying a soft-deleted Person or Company through its full-page command menu succeeds but leaves the destroyed record displayed with unusable Restore controls.
bugs.expected: After successful permanent destruction, the full record page should leave the destroyed record and stop offering restoration.
bugs.actual: The destroy operation removes the record, but the original full-page URL still displays its name, deleted banner and Restore buttons. Restore does not recover it. Ordinary list navigation remains usable.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Person and open its full record page.
Soft-delete the Person, then open the full-page command menu through the header menu or keyboard shortcut.
Choose Permanently destroy Person and confirm destruction.
Observe that the page stays at the destroyed record with the deleted banner and Restore controls; restoration does not recover the record.
Verify the Person is absent from live and deleted-record lists. Repeat with another fresh Person.
Control: ordinary soft deletion followed by Restore works; destroying a record from its actual record side panel closes that panel and leaves the list usable.

bugs.name: Canceled events appear as active meetings in record Calendar rows
bugs.summary: Record Calendar rows omit cancellation state and render canceled event titles without the intended strikethrough.
bugs.expected: A Calendar row for an event whose saved isCanceled flag is true should apply the component’s cancellation styling, distinguishing it from active events.
bugs.actual: Existing canceled events render plain titles before and after reload, indistinguishable from noncanceled controls. Direct event readbacks preserve isCanceled=true, but the Calendar timeline query omits that field.
reproSteps: On a disposable fixture, locate an existing canceled event linked to a visible Person or Company and a noncanceled event control. Independently verify their saved isCanceled values; do not create or cancel calendar data.
Open the linked record’s Calendar tab and locate the canceled event. Its readable title has no strikethrough.
Reload and reopen the Calendar tab. The canceled title remains plain, matching the active control’s title presentation.
Repeat with another canceled event or linked record. Compare the Calendar row with the event’s saved cancellation flag.

bugs.name: Rejected saved Linkedin edits provide no explanatory validation feedback
bugs.summary: An invalid edit to an existing Person Linkedin link is refused while the editor provides no explanation.
bugs.expected: An explicit save refused for invalid URL input should explain the validation failure and preserve the saved link.
bugs.actual: Replacing a saved Linkedin link with not-a-url and pressing Enter leaves the editor open with the invalid draft, no explanatory text or notification, and the original saved link unchanged. Valid corrections save and persist. An initially empty link field displays its error outline, while the populated editor remains neutral.
reproSteps: Create a Person and save a valid Linkedin URL.
Reopen its Linkedin editor, replace the edit draft with not-a-url and press Enter.
Observe the editor stays open without explanatory validation feedback. Escape and reload to confirm the original valid URL remains.
Repeat on another fresh Person. Compare a valid replacement, which saves and persists, and an invalid initially empty link field, which displays its error outline.

bugs.name: Create link opens an unusable URL form for the first paragraph in a narrow Note or Task editor
bugs.summary: At a narrow viewport, the Note or Task formatting toolbar’s Create link action fails to expose a usable URL form for first-paragraph selections.
bugs.expected: Clicking Create link for selected Note text should expose a usable URL form.
bugs.actual: At 390px width, selecting the first paragraph and clicking Create link preserves the text highlight and toolbar but shows no usable URL input. The form is mounted with display:none. The same Note at desktop width, or a lower paragraph at the same narrow width, exposes Edit URL and can save a link. A narrow Task editor also leaves the first-paragraph Create link URL form invisible or unusable; its desktop and lower-paragraph controls work.
reproSteps: Create a Note with a short first paragraph and save it. At 390px width, select that paragraph.
Click Create link in the formatting toolbar. Observe no URL form appears despite the retained selection and toolbar.
Repeat on another fresh Note, including plain unformatted text.
Compare the same first paragraph at desktop width and a lower paragraph at 390px: Edit URL appears and valid links can be saved and retained after reload.

Additional verified variation: Use the same Create link toolbar action on the first paragraph of a narrow Task editor. Open a fresh Task editor at 390px width and enter first-paragraph text. Select that paragraph and click the visible Create link toolbar button. Observe the unusable URL form; compare the desktop layout and lower-paragraph selection.

bugs.name: Extensionless Company file rejection incorrectly reports a permission denial
bugs.summary: A filename-extension validation error appears as Access denied despite working upload permissions.
bugs.expected: An invalid filename should receive feedback consistent with its validation failure rather than falsely indicating missing upload permission.
bugs.actual: Uploading a nonempty extensionless file through Company Files shows a red Access denied toast and leaves Files empty. The internal error identifies the missing extension. Uploading the same content with .txt succeeds and remains after reload.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Company and open its Files tab.
Use Add file to upload a nonempty file with no filename extension. Observe Access denied and no attachment.
Repeat on another fresh Company and reload to confirm the rejected file was not saved.
Upload the same content with a .txt extension through the same control. Observe the attachment is present after reload.

bugs.name: Relinking a Task or Note hides its existing Company creation history
bugs.summary: Relinking a recently unlinked Task or Note can rewrite its creation Timeline row into an empty diff, hiding that history while the activity remains linked.
bugs.expected: Relinking an activity preserves its already-visible creation history rather than silently hiding the row.
bugs.actual: A creation row remains visible after unlink, but disappears after relink and reload. Tasks or Notes still contains the live linked item, while Timeline retains the related-deletion row. The creation event still exists; its properties change from {} to {diff:{}}.
reproSteps: Create a disposable Company and a related Task; verify its creation row in Company Timeline.
Unlink the Company from the Task and verify the creation row still exists. Relink the same Company as the same member shortly after creation.
Reload and compare Company Timeline with its Tasks tab. Repeat with a Note.
Compare an isolated relink after the recent-event window, and retain any intervening-event controls that do not reproduce.

bugs.name: Mobile record header ellipsis covers the end of its record counter
bugs.summary: A long record title can collapse the header’s action-button column, placing the ellipsis over the record-position counter.
bugs.expected: The normal record header keeps its position/total counter readable beside the Command Menu button.
bugs.actual: At 390px with a long record title, the header gives the action column zero width and its Command Menu button overlaps the right end of the counter. The same record at desktop width and a short-title Company at 390px are clear. The menu still opens.
reproSteps: Create a disposable Company with a long title and open its full record at 390px width.
Inspect the record-position counter at the right end of the breadcrumb beside the ellipsis button. Repeat from another load.
Compare the same record at desktop width and a short-title record at 390px; open the Command Menu to verify it remains usable.

bugs.name: Linking Note text makes its Body preview omit that text
bugs.summary: After the only paragraph in a Note becomes a hyperlink, its editor still shows the text but the saved Fields Body preview becomes blank after reload. Plain text remains visible; a partially linked paragraph omits its linked fragment.
bugs.expected: Applying a supported hyperlink should preserve the linked text in the plain-text Body preview.
bugs.actual: After the only paragraph in a Note becomes a hyperlink, its editor still shows the text but the saved Fields Body preview becomes blank after reload. Plain text remains visible; a partially linked paragraph omits its linked fragment.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Note with a plain paragraph and confirm its Body preview.
Select the paragraph and create a hyperlink, save and reload.
Compare the visible editor text with the blank Fields Body preview; repeat on a separate Note and retain a plain-text control.

bugs.name: Rejected saved Phone edits lack an explanatory message
bugs.summary: Explicitly saving a validator-refused edit to a saved Person Phone leaves a pale red outline and the editor open without explanatory text or toast. The previous saved number remains; a valid replacement saves normally.
bugs.expected: An explicitly refused Phone save should explain its validation failure rather than relying on a subtle outline alone.
bugs.actual: Explicitly saving a validator-refused edit to a saved Person Phone leaves a pale red outline and the editor open without explanatory text or toast. The previous saved number remains; a valid replacement saves normally.
reproSteps: Open a fresh Person with a saved Phone and attempt an invalid phone edit through its normal editor.
Explicitly save and inspect feedback: the editor remains open with an outline but no explanation.
Reload to verify the original number remains; compare a valid replacement and repeat with fresh data.

bugs.name: Timeline stops updating after a same-record panel transition
bugs.summary: After opening the same Company from its side panel into the full record page with overlapping Timeline instances, changing Annual Revenue updates Fields but the Timeline stays at its earlier history. Reload shows the saved changes.
bugs.expected: The mounted Timeline should receive and display subsequent record updates as promised by its real-time update contract.
bugs.actual: After opening the same Company from its side panel into the full record page with overlapping Timeline instances, changing Annual Revenue updates Fields but the Timeline stays at its earlier history. Reload shows the saved changes.
reproSteps: Open an owned Company in a record side panel with its Timeline mounted.
Transition the same Company into the full record page while the panel lifecycle overlaps.
Change Annual Revenue and compare the updated Field with the unchanged Timeline; reload to reveal the saved history. Repeat the targeted transition and compare an ordinary mounted Timeline control.

bugs.name: Deleted record breadcrumb keeps the active-record total
bugs.summary: Deleting a Company leaves the deleted banner with its previous active-record rank/total, such as 1/610. Reload changes it to the deleted-only 1/1 or 1/2; a fresh Person shows the same stale-total defect.
bugs.expected: A deleted record breadcrumb should show rank and total among deleted records.
bugs.actual: Deleting a Company leaves the deleted banner with its previous active-record rank/total, such as 1/610. Reload changes it to the deleted-only 1/1 or 1/2; a fresh Person shows the same stale-total defect.
reproSteps: Create and open a disposable Company.
Delete it through the record command and compare its deleted banner with the retained breadcrumb total.
Reload to observe the deleted-only total. Repeat with fresh data; compare opening and dismissing the menu without deleting.

bugs.name: Deleting a related Task omits its Timeline removal history
bugs.summary: Deleting related Tasks removes them from Company Tasks, but after refresh the Company Timeline has no removal entry. Explicitly unlinking a live control Task creates the expected relationship-removal entry. Existing creation links may become Untitled but still open the correct deleted Task.
bugs.expected: Company activity history should represent removal of the relationship caused by Task deletion consistently with explicit unlinking.
bugs.actual: Deleting related Tasks removes them from Company Tasks, but after refresh the Company Timeline has no removal entry. Explicitly unlinking a live control Task creates the expected relationship-removal entry. Existing creation links may become Untitled but still open the correct deleted Task.
reproSteps: Create fresh Companies with related Tasks and verify their creation history.
Delete one Task through its normal record command, then refresh the Company Timeline and Tasks.
Repeat with another fresh Task and compare a live control Task removed only from its Company relation.

bugs.name: Cleared Currency Timeline value omits the Empty label
bugs.summary: After successfully clearing Company Annual Revenue, Timeline displays a blank destination after the change arrow instead of Empty. Reload retains the blank label. An ordinary Name clear displays Empty and a revenue value of 0 renders 0.
bugs.expected: A saved empty Currency change should have the same intelligible empty-value presentation as the ordinary empty-field control.
bugs.actual: After successfully clearing Company Annual Revenue, Timeline displays a blank destination after the change arrow instead of Empty. Reload retains the blank label. An ordinary Name clear displays Empty and a revenue value of 0 renders 0.
reproSteps: Create a Company with Annual Revenue and save it.
Clear Annual Revenue through the normal record editor and let the save finish.
Inspect the Timeline change before and after reload; compare an ordinary Name clear and a 0 revenue value.

bugs.name: Email edit saves a malformed comma-suffix address
bugs.summary: Editing a Person Email to a whole comma-suffix string saves it and reopening after reload displays the same complete malformed string. A valid replacement saves; not-an-email and a pair of complete addresses are refused.
bugs.expected: The email editor should reject malformed single-address strings consistently with its valid-format validation.
bugs.actual: Editing a Person Email to a whole comma-suffix string saves it and reopening after reload displays the same complete malformed string. A valid replacement saves; not-an-email and a pair of complete addresses are refused.
reproSteps: Create a fresh Person and edit its normal Email field to qa-email-check@example.invalid,not-an-email. Repeat with another fresh Person and a unique equivalent value, such as qa-email-check-b@example.invalid,not-an-email.
Save, reload and reopen the editor to inspect the entire persisted rendered value.
Compare a valid replacement, a plain invalid string and two complete addresses.

bugs.name: Escape commits an attachment rename instead of cancelling it
bugs.summary: Pressing Escape during a Company attachment rename commits the pending filename, which persists after reload.
bugs.expected: Escape should leave attachment rename mode and discard the pending filename edit, preserving the saved filename.
bugs.actual: Edited filenames persist after Escape and reload. Independent recordings and the original reconstructed replay support the observed save.
reproSteps: Upload a valid attachment to a Company and begin renaming it.
Edit the filename, press Escape and reload.

bugs.name: Overdue due date not highlighted for In progress tasks
bugs.summary: In the record Tasks tab, a past-due task's due date is shown in red while status is To do, but loses the overdue (red) styling as soon as status changes to In progress, even though the task is still not done.
bugs.expected: Due dates in the past should be highlighted as overdue for any task that is not Done (To do and In progress).
bugs.actual: Due date Oct 15, 2026 (today is Oct 28, 2026) shows red under TODO group, but is rendered in normal grey under IN_PROGRESS group.
reproSteps: Open a Company record’s Tasks tab and create a disposable Task.
Set its Due Date to a day in the past and Status to To do. Confirm the date has red overdue styling.
Change Status to In progress and observe the date change to normal styling. Reload to confirm.
Change Status back to To do and compare the restored overdue styling.

bugs.name: Company Emails tab shows threads out of date order once more pages load
bugs.summary: On a company's Emails tab, the first 20 threads are newest-first. Each further page loaded by scrolling is sorted only within itself, so newer threads show up below older ones. The list is not in one chronological order.
bugs.expected: All threads are sorted newest-first across the whole list. A thread dated Oct 25 never appears below threads dated Oct 16 or Sep 24.
bugs.actual: Dates in display order (company SLB, 84 threads): Oct 28 … Oct 17, Oct 16, Oct 16, then **Oct 25**, Oct 20, … Sep 24, then **Oct 23**, Oct 23, … Sep 3, then **Oct 25**, Oct 24, … Aug 10, then **Oct 11**, Oct 9, Aug 21, Aug 18. Each block of 20 is sorted, but each new block starts with recent dates again.
reproSteps: Open a seeded Company whose Emails tab contains more than one page of threads.
Inspect the visible dates on the first page, then scroll to load subsequent pages.
Compare the last displayed dates of each page with the next page’s first dates. Observe newer threads appended below older threads.

bugs.name: Opening a company from its side panel removes the Tasks creation action
bugs.summary: When a company's side panel is displaying Tasks and the user clicks Open, the full record retains task cards but loses the Tasks header/count and New task button. Switching tabs restores them.
bugs.expected: The full company record's Tasks tab keeps its header and New task action when opened from the side panel.
bugs.actual: The New task action and Tasks heading/count are missing until the user changes tabs or reloads.
reproSteps: Open a task linked to a company and open the Company relation in the side panel.
Select Tasks and confirm the header, count and New task action appear.
Click Open at the side-panel footer. The full company page retains task cards but loses the Tasks header and creation action.
Switch to Timeline and back to Tasks, or reload; the header and action return.

bugs.name: Edit Layout from a note side panel opens the company layout editor
bugs.summary: Edit Layout in a related Note side panel targets the underlying Company layout instead of the Note layout.
bugs.expected: Edit Layout should target the Notes record layout from which the action was invoked.
bugs.actual: The Note side panel closes and Companies layout edition opens, showing the underlying company fields and tabs. The report describes two reproductions.
reproSteps: Open a Company record and its Notes tab.
Open a related Note in the side panel.
Open the Note side panel Options menu, alongside Delete Note and Export Note.
Choose Edit Layout and observe that the Companies layout editor opens instead of the Notes layout editor.

bugs.name: Note and task body edits are permanently lost on immediate tab switches
bugs.summary: Pending Note and Task body edits disappear when switching immediately to Timeline and remain missing after returning and reloading.
bugs.expected: Switching tabs should flush pending body edits or retain them until autosave completes.
bugs.actual: A newly appended paragraph vanishes on returning from Timeline and remains absent after reload. The report reproduces the loss on a standalone Note and a Task, with no warning.
reproSteps: Open a standalone Note or Task and enter body text, allowing it to save.
Append a new paragraph and immediately click Timeline.
Return to the body tab and observe that the appended paragraph is already missing.
Reload to confirm persistence loss. Repeat on the other activity type.

bugs.name: Inline note file's Download button opens a preview instead of downloading
bugs.summary: The explicit inline Note file Download action opens a raw-text preview, while Files downloads the same newly uploaded attachment.
bugs.expected: Download file should trigger a browser download, consistently with the Files-tab Download action.
bugs.actual: For a freshly uploaded .txt attachment, the inline toolbar action opens a new raw-text tab without a download. Files, attachment More options, Download successfully downloads the same file with matching bytes. The report reproduces it twice.
reproSteps: Open a Note and insert a File block using the slash menu. Upload a fresh .txt attachment.
Select the inline file block and click Download file in its toolbar.
Observe a new raw-text preview tab instead of a download.
Use Files, the same attachment More options, Download as a control; confirm it downloads successfully.
